It is also a well-known CoO2-cathode coating, so it should give a low interfacial penalty at 4.0 V.

Br- is more polarizable and easier to oxidize than Cl-, so the penalty may be higher than the chloride analogs, but the bromide is a chemically distinct test of the halide family.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (0.337), LiF (0.310), Li6Zr2O7 (0.743) and Li3BO3 (0.725) all showed large sulfide-driven penalties. The Li2MgCl4 and Li2ZnCl4 chlorides were best at about 0.189 (bin 9), so the halide family is the most promising. The mp-aaacdofg LiBr polymorph is the only remaining available halide that is not a fluoride or a mixed-cation halide.

proposal.hypothesis: LiCaAlF6 is a wide-gap mixed-metal fluoride built on Al3+ and Ca2+, both very hard to reduce. The fluoride anion is hard to oxidize, so it should avoid the strong P/S and Zr/S exchange seen with the oxides. LiF, the simplest fluoride, still gave a 0.31 eV penalty, so a more electrochemically robust multication fluoride is worth testing. The chlorides remain the best family but no chloride is available in the candidate list.
proposal.motivation: Li2MgCl4 and Li2ZnCl4 gave the lowest penalty (0.189, bin 9), but no chloride remains in the available list. Oxide and simple fluoride contacts gave 0.31 eV or higher, so a different fluoride with non-reducible Al3+ and Ca2+ cations is the next option.
